articles.title: Alex Pereira Should NOT Be the Underdog Against Sergei Pavlovich
articles.description: Use my code CHAEL to get up to 50% off your Hume Pod: https://sponsr.is/humehealth_chael Sergei Pavlovich is a 2-to-1 favorite over Alex Pereira, and Chael says the line is built on an idea that is not true: there is no size advantage in stand-up fighting. Size matters in wrestling, Chael says, but Muhammad Ali won Olympic heavyweight gold at 198 pounds, Mike Tyson at 220 never had a size advantage over a single opponent except Jake Paul, and Roy Jones Jr., Terence Crawford, and Floyd Mayweather all beat bigger men by being smaller, faster, and better on their feet. Chael re-watches the Ciryl Gane fight and says it is not what you remember. Gane swarmed Pereira with a performance he never attempted against Jon Jones or Francis Ngannou, and Pereira never got his own offense started. Pavlovich can swarm the same way, and his hands are good enough that his wrestling rarely shows, but Chael does not think that wrestling overwhelms Pereira, so this becomes a stand-up fight between a former kickboxing world champion and a wrestler who learned to box. The part Chael cannot let go of: Pereira has already said that if this does not work out he will go back to 205, and Daniel Cormier doubled down on it four days ago. If any part of Pereira is already planning the exit, Chael says, he is up against it. Subscribe for more from Chael on MMA, wrestling, and the fights that matter. articles.title: Josh Hokit Reveals What Happened in the Hospital With Ciryl Gane
articles.description: Thanks to Bear Mattress for sponsoring this video! ​Visit https://bearmattress.com/chael and use CODE: chael to get 40% off your Bear mattress! Josh Hokit sat down with Michael Bisping and admitted what pains him: Ciryl Gane is a nice guy. Not just nice, cool, a gentleman, and Chael says he had the exact same experience. He did not want to like Gane either, and then he met him. Chael retells the faceoff story: Hokit tells Gane, "I thought you'd be taller," and throws out an Egyptian word meant to deeply offend him, except Gane has never heard it and genuinely wants to understand the insult so he can measure how angry he should be. Then the part nobody saw: both men ended up in the emergency room after the fight, on gurneys next to each other, and Gane told Hokit, "You're going to be world champion someday." Hokit's answer: "I need that belt now." Chael also gets into why he loves watching a Hokit interview, never knowing whether he is getting the entertainer or the real Josh, and closes with the Dave Schultz and Pat Smith story: the older champion who beat the younger man, then picked him up in tears in the parking lot. Subscribe for more from Chael on MMA, wrestling, and the fights that matter. articles.title: Bruce Lee Or Mark Zuckerberg? Chael Answers
articles.description: Thanks to Bear Mattress for sponsoring this video! ​Visit https://bearmattress.com/chael and use CODE: chael to get 40% off your Bear mattress! It is Ask Uncle Chael, and the questions cover everything. Chael starts with Thanksgiving, and whether Roy Nelson would ever let a macaroni green bean casserole past him in line. Then it gets serious: Bruce Lee or Mark Zuckerberg is not the easy fight you think, because Zuckerberg can actually fight, he is just too passive, and Chael says one coaching change, never take a step backward, would jump him levels in a day. Chael does not hold back on Wing Chun, calling it a complete waste of time for anyone who thinks it is a combat art, and he settles prime Team Quest against prime Blackzilians honestly: on paper Team Quest, with two UFC belts, two Pride belts, and the number one ranked fighter in the world at the same time, could not be matched, even if the sport should have passed them by. There is also the full story of Frank, the fighter Chael owed one to, who booked his own ticket a day early and planned to sleep at Portland airport for 23 hours rather than miss his shot, plus Chael's blunt answer on Greco-Roman wrestling: as a Greco man himself, he says it is not popular anywhere, and he competed in front of two mothers to prove it. He closes on Gable Steveson, and what a second straight loss would actually do to his UFC career. Subscribe for more from Chael on MMA, wrestling, and the fights that matter. articles.title: Islam Says Two More Fights. Chael Has A Theory
articles.description: Use my code CHAEL to get up to 50% off your Hume Pod: https://sponsr.is/humehealth_chael There is a phenomenon in MMA Chael cannot quite put his finger on: the moment a champion has tremendous success, all he wants is out. Islam Makhachev is going through it now. He has said he will do two more fights, and Chael appreciates the honesty, but announcing it takes away the thing that made Khabib's retirement the single greatest moment Chael has ever seen in the sport. Khabib was supposed to go 30-0, with number 30 a business fight, a second McGregor fight, and instead he took the microphone after beating Gaethje and retired, and the surprise is why it still lands all these years later. Islam saying two more removes that, unless he pulls the double cross. And the critics have already started: say two more and the first thing you hear is that you are scared of Usman Nurmagomedov. Chael closes with a conversation he had with Kyle Dake, who told him why MMA's top guys are exhausted while Dake, taking on twenty men a year, is not: they sit around and fight their matches mentally and emotionally, multiple times a day. Dake never thinks about it at all. Subscribe for more from Chael on MMA, wrestling, and the fights that matter. articles.title: Should the UFC Sign Usman After the Merab Incident? #ufc
articles.description: Should the UFC sign Usman following the incident involving Merab Dvalishvili? Chael Sonnen questions whether the UFC's interest in signing Usman should be affected by what happened. Merab has reportedly said the two are on good terms, that he has forgiven Usman, and that he wants others to do the same. Chael isn't defending what happened. He makes it clear that he believes Usman's actions were wrong. But he also points out that Usman has already faced serious consequences, including time in prison and potentially never being allowed back into the country. Should the UFC add to those consequences, or is it time to let the situation move forward? Chael makes the case that accountability matters, but so does recognizing when someone has already been punished. #UFC #MerabDvalishvili #KamaruUsman #MMA #UFCNews #ChaelSonnen

articles.title: Josh Hokit’s Takedown Was Crazy #ufc
articles.description: Chael Sonnen doesn't expect this to be a close fight. In his mind, somebody is going to get dominated, and Josh Hokit's wrestling could determine who. Before Josh fought Derrick Lewis, Chael had one major question: Could Hokit actually get a heavyweight opponent to the ground when he needed to? That question didn't last long. Chael recalls watching Hokit take down Derrick Lewis so quickly that he had to replay the sequence multiple times. Eventually, he realized the takedown was happening too fast for him to even break down what he was seeing. Now, Chael sees that explosive wrestling as a major weapon and believes it could make all the difference in Josh's next matchup. #JoshHokit #DerrickLewis #UFC #MMA #ChaelSonnen #Wrestling If you send the rest of the transcript, I can make sure the package captures the full argument rather than just the takedown setup.

articles.title: Matthew McConaughey Is LYING About His Tuna Salad
articles.description: Chael Sonnen has tried to let this go, but Matthew McConaughey's tuna salad story has finally pushed him too far. McConaughey has shared his unusual tuna recipe on multiple podcasts, complete with wasabi, guava, frozen peas, corn and crushed potato chips. Chael has one problem: he doesn't believe McConaughey has ever actually made it. From the ingredients supposedly sitting in his refrigerator to putting crushed chips into tuna and leaving it overnight, Chael breaks down every part of the story—and explains why Bert Kreischer's reaction might bother him even more than the recipe itself. And somehow, Woody Harrelson gets dragged into this.

articles.title: Jon Jones Does NOT Understand the Fight Business
articles.description: Jon Jones says the idea of coming back and beating someone up one more time sounds appealing. Chael Sonnen believes Jones is missing the reality of his current position. According to Chael, the UFC has already moved on. The heavyweight division has a champion, Jones no longer holds the belt, and simply wanting another fight isn't enough. If Jones truly wants back in, Chael believes he needs to identify an opponent, Ciryl Gane, Tom Aspinall, Alex Pereira, or Josh Hokit and give the UFC a story it can actually sell. More importantly, Chael explains why keeping Jones under contract may be more valuable to the UFC than actually booking him to fight—and why Jones may be misunderstanding the business leverage he still has.

articles.title: Josh Hokit Wants Consequences: "I Have To Poke Him"
articles.description: Josh Hokit walked into Madison Square Garden 10-0 and walked out with his first loss. Ciryl Gane kept the UFC heavyweight title at UFC 334, winning a unanimous decision (48-47 on all three cards) after landing 237 significant strikes, the most ever by one fighter in a UFC heavyweight fight. Hokit landed 146. Somewhere in that war, a Gane finger went into Hokit's eye and no point was taken. After the fight, with his vision still blurry, Hokit took to Instagram with a message for the champion: "There has to be consequences next time." He wants an immediate rematch, and Dana White, who admits he's had his issues with Hokit, came away calling him "the real deal." 0:00 Hokit's warning 0:10 His first loss 0:20 UFC 334: Gane vs Hokit 0:33 Dana White: "He fought the perfect fight" 0:51 Record strikes, the decision and the eye poke 1:13 Dana White: "Unbelievable chin, unstoppable cardio" 1:41 Hokit's Instagram message: "There has to be consequences" 2:28 The rematch push and Dana's verdict Should the UFC run it back right away?
